findings.description: Unsafe pickle deserialization via pickle.loads() with user-controlled data
findings.reasoning: The function load_str_bytes() calls pickle.loads(bb) on line 42 when proto == Protocol.pickle and allow_pickle=True. The 'bb' variable comes from user-provided 'b' parameter (str or bytes). An attacker can provide a malicious pickle payload that will execute arbitrary code during deserialization. While allow_pickle defaults to False, if a caller sets allow_pickle=True or if content_type ends with 'pickle' and allow_pickle=True, arbitrary pickle deserialization occurs. This is a classic unsafe deserialization vulnerability (CWE-502).

evidence.dataflow_analysis: The 'b' parameter (type StrBytes) is user-controlled input. When proto == Protocol.pickle and allow_pickle=True, the code calls pickle.loads(bb) where bb is derived from b (either b itself if bytes, or b.encode() if string). No validation or sanitization of the pickle data occurs before deserialization.
evidence.notes: The vulnerability exists in the load_str_bytes function. The load_file function also calls load_str_bytes, potentially exposing file-based deserialization. The default allow_pickle=False provides some protection, but the vulnerability exists when allow_pickle=True.
